issue_context.title: System.Text.Json unsafe and ref struct serialization exceptions
issue_context.body:
Understandably Span and friends or pointers will not be supported but it shouldn't cause exceptions like this, it would be useful to at least have the offending property path.

This may have already been fixed, I couldn't find any related issues.

SDK: 3.1.102

Serializing Memory<byte> (has a Span property)
```
System.TypeLoadException: The generic type 'System.Text.Json.JsonPropertyInfoNotNullable`4' was used with an invalid instantiation in assembly 'System.Text.Json, Version=4.0.1.1, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51'.
   at System.RuntimeType.MakeGenericType(Type[] instantiation)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonClassInfo.CreateProperty(Type declaredPropertyType, Type runtimePropertyType, Type implementedPropertyType, PropertyInfo propertyInfo, Type parentClassType, JsonConverter converter, JsonSerializerOptions options)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonClassInfo.AddProperty(Type propertyType, PropertyInfo propertyInfo, Type classType, JsonSerializerOptions options)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonClassInfo..ctor(Type type, JsonSerializerOptions options)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions.GetOrAddClass(Type classType)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonPropertyInfo.get_RuntimeClassInfo()
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Write(Utf8JsonWriter writer, Int32 originalWriterDepth, Int32 flushThreshold, JsonSerializerOptions options, WriteStack& state)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.WriteAsyncCore(Stream utf8Json, Object value, Type inputType, JsonSerializerOptions options, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
```

Serializing:

```cs
public class Foo 
{
    public unsafe int* Bar {get;}
}
```
```
System.ArgumentException: The type 'System.Int32*' may not be used as a type argument.
   at System.RuntimeType.ThrowIfTypeNeverValidGenericArgument(RuntimeType type)
   at System.RuntimeType.SanityCheckGenericArguments(RuntimeType[] genericArguments, RuntimeType[] genericParamters)
   at System.RuntimeType.MakeGenericType(Type[] instantiation)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonClassInfo.CreateProperty(Type declaredPropertyType, Type runtimePropertyType, Type implementedPropertyType, PropertyInfo propertyInfo, Type parentClassType, JsonConverter converter, JsonSerializerOptions options)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonClassInfo.AddProperty(Type propertyType, PropertyInfo propertyInfo, Type classType, JsonSerializerOptions options)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonClassInfo..ctor(Type type, JsonSerializerOptions options)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions.GetOrAddClass(Type classType)
   at System.Text.Json.WriteStackFrame.Initialize(Type type, JsonSerializerOptions options)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.WriteAsyncCore(Stream utf8Json, Object value, Type inputType, JsonSerializerOptions options, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
```

review_comments: When was this attribute introduced?  If it was at the same time as IsByRefLike, any reason not to just use reflection to look for IsByRefLike and invoke it rather than looking for this attribute?

Can you add a test case for `Memory<T>` as well please (for both serialize and deserialize)? 

~Also, just for completeness, add a test for `Utf8JsonReader` (a ref-struct type containing another ref-struct as a field).~
**Edit:** Never mind, I see you have that covered already as part of `RefStructTypes`. Nice :)
A test for `Memory<T>` is included in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/d0b6b3f52b94b81e60784c831c9a9c8a16ed1e2c/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/tests/Serialization/InvalidTypeTests.cs#L56.

Why is `PropertyInfo` nullable here? Maybe add a `Debug.Assert` before the last throw statement if we know for sure  that if `parentClassType` is not null, then` propertyInfo` is not null. I want to make sure we don't have accidental null ref here.

`parentClassType` & `propertyInfo` will both be `null` when an invalid type is detected during the creation of a `JsonClassInfo` info for the type.

If an invalid type is detected as the return type of a property on a POCO (when creating `JsonPropertyInfo`s), then `parentClassType` and `propertyInfo` will both not be `null`.

I added an assert that `propertyInfo` is `null` when `parentClassInfo` is `null`.

Not sure adding a `Debug.Assert` right before the last throw adds much value, as there'll be a null ref anyway (which will be encountered in debug mode) if `propertyInfo` is null.
Does the result of this end up getting cached at a higher-level?  Just want to make sure we're not incurring this reflection on every operation.
Yes. This information is fetched once per type to (de)serialize (during warm up), and won't be fetched again on subsequent (de)serialization operations.
